score_100.reason: Fig. 5M shows the effect of bilateral chemogenetic inhibition of OB-projecting cholinergic neurons on olfactory discrimination learning and its reversibility. The core is to understand the DREADD experimental design, the meanings of the two Two-way ANOVA significance annotations, and the causal interpretation of acute modulation rather than long-term plasticity disruption. The graph contains three learning curves and is worth 30 points. Bilateral injection, CNO administration, and statistical design are worth 25 points. The scientific interpretation is split into two items: bilateral hM4D(Gi)+CNO inhibition impairs learning, worth 25 points, and rapid recovery after CNO cessation supports acute reversible modulation, worth 20 points. Point allocation: graph reproduction 30, experimental design and statistics 25, learning-impairment conclusion 25, reversibility conclusion 20.

rubric.GT core conclusion: Fig. 5M shows that bilateral chemogenetic inhibition of OB-projecting cholinergic neurons significantly impairs olfactory discrimination learning. During the nine CNO training sessions from Day 1 to Day 17, the hM4D(Gi)+CNO group has a significantly lower success rate than the mCherry+CNO control group, while both groups still improve across training days. After CNO is stopped, the hM4D(Gi) group rapidly recovers to control-level performance during Days 19-21. The core conclusion is that OB-projecting cholinergic neurons causally contribute to normal olfactory discrimination learning, and that the deficit mainly reflects acute, reversible loss of cholinergic modulation rather than permanent disruption of long-term synaptic plasticity.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly analyzes and visualizes the three learning curves: blue hM4D(Gi)+CNO and pink mCherry+CNO cover Days 1-17, magenta hM4D(Gi) no-CNO covers Days 19-21, curves show mean +/- SEM, the x-axis is training day, the y-axis is success rate, horizontal and vertical significance markers are annotated, and the trends match the original figure showing impaired learning in the hM4D(Gi)+CNO group and recovery after CNO cessation.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct the full 30 points if the panel is misidentified as a pie chart, scatter plot, heatmap, neural activity trace, or single-session behavioral result. Deduct 10 points if any one of the three curves is missing. Deduct 8 points if the CNO training period and no-CNO recovery period are not distinguished. Deduct 6 points if mean +/- SEM or significance markers are missing. Deduct 12 points if the y-axis is not success rate or the trend direction is wrong.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly explains the experimental design and statistical analysis: hM4D(Gi)-mCherry or mCherry is injected bilaterally, CNO is injected intraperitoneally about 30 minutes before each training session at 5 mg/kg, Days 1-17 include nine CNO training sessions, and Two-way ANOVA on Days 1-17 tests group and day factors; the horizontal sigstar corresponds to the day effect and the vertical sigstar corresponds to the group effect.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 6 points if bilateral injection is not described. Deduct 8 points if CNO administration or the training period is not described. Deduct 8 points if the mCherry control group and hM4D(Gi) group are confused. Deduct 8 points if the group and day factors in the Two-way ANOVA are not described. Deduct 6 points if the meanings of horizontal and vertical sigstars are reversed.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly explains the core conclusion that bilateral inhibition impairs learning: during Days 1-17, the hM4D(Gi)+CNO group has a significantly lower success rate than the mCherry+CNO control group, the group effect is significant, and OB-projecting cholinergic neurons therefore make a causal contribution to olfactory discrimination learning; the significant day effect indicates that training days still improve performance.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 20 points if the hM4D(Gi)+CNO group is claimed to be unaffected or to outperform the control group. Deduct 10 points if the significant group effect is not linked to learning impairment by inhibition. Deduct 6 points if the day effect or improvement across training is not described. Deduct 8 points if the result is interpreted as correlational rather than causal manipulation evidence.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly explains the reversibility conclusion: after CNO cessation, the hM4D(Gi) group rapidly recovers to control-level success rates during the three training sessions on Days 19-21, indicating that the behavioral deficit is caused by acute CNO-mediated cholinergic inhibition rather than permanent disruption of long-term synaptic plasticity or learning capacity.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 10 points if the recovery phase after CNO cessation is not described. Deduct 12 points if the deficit is claimed to be irreversible or to persist through the no-CNO phase. Deduct 8 points if the response does not explain that recovery supports acute modulation rather than long-term plasticity disruption. Deduct 5 points if the panel is overstated as identifying all downstream mechanisms.

Acceptable deviations: It is acceptable to describe OB-projecting cholinergic neurons as cholinergic neurons projecting to the olfactory bulb.
It is acceptable to describe hM4D(Gi) as an inhibitory DREADD or chemogenetic inhibition tool.
It is acceptable to describe CNO administration as pre-training or acute CNO administration.
Success rate may be described as behavioral success rate or percent correct.
The exact Two-way ANOVA p-values need not be written in scientific notation as long as significant group effect and significant day effect are correctly stated.
It is acceptable to describe the recovery phase as Days 19-21 or three sessions after CNO withdrawal.
It is acceptable to describe acute modulation as ongoing acute modulation or reversible modulation.
rubric.Scoring instructions: High scores (85-100) require correctly reproducing the three learning curves, explaining bilateral DREADD injection, CNO administration, and the meanings of the Two-way ANOVA annotations, accurately stating that the hM4D(Gi)+CNO group has impaired learning, and explaining that rapid recovery after CNO cessation indicates acute reversible loss of modulation rather than long-term plasticity disruption. Partial scores (40-84) should be assigned when the graph trend and learning-impairment direction are correct but experimental design, statistics, or reversibility interpretation is incomplete. Low scores (0-39) should be assigned when the panel is confused with a non-learning curve, experimental and control groups are mixed up, the opposite conclusion that inhibition has no effect is drawn, or the recovery phase is ignored.
